AlertFiringDetail.description:
Heavyweight per-firing view for the drawer/drill-down screen.

Intentionally separate from ``AlertFiring`` so the list endpoint stays
cheap — loading every trigger payload and joining rules for a table
render would turn the History tab into a pull-the-world query.
AlertFiringDetail.title: AlertFiringDetail

AlertRuleUpdate.description:
Partial edit surface for an alert rule. ``enabled`` is deliberately
absent — use ``PATCH /rules/{id}/enabled`` for the on/off toggle so
the two code paths don't silently race on the same row.
AlertRuleUpdate.title: AlertRuleUpdate

AlertsConfig.description:
Slice 13: external alert delivery + default-rule seeding.

``webhook_url`` toggles the :class:`WebhookAlertNotifier`. Empty (the
default) keeps the engine on the :class:`NullAlertNotifier` so existing
tests and dev-mode runs don't try to reach a non-existent endpoint.

``notifier_format`` picks between a generic JSON payload (``"webhook"``,
default) and a Slack-compatible ``{"text": "..."}`` shape (``"slack"``).
``webhook_token`` is sent as ``Authorization: Bearer <token>`` when
non-empty; the secret never appears in any log line.
AlertsConfig.title: AlertsConfig

AuditEntry.description:
Shape of one audit_log row as it comes back from the API.

``before`` / ``after`` are free-form JSON snapshots so they keep
``extra="allow"`` semantics on the payload objects themselves; the
entry envelope is still strict.
AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry

BulkOperationError.description:
Per-item failure carried inside :class:`BulkOperationResult`.

Bulk operations capture per-row failures rather than aborting the
whole batch — operators running an incident-response action need to
see partial state. ``error_code`` is the exception class name (not
the message) so the wire format stays small and predictable; the
full traceback lands in the daemon's structlog feed.
BulkOperationError.title: BulkOperationError

BulkOperationResult.description:
Outcome envelope for bulk pause / mark-expired calls.

``paused_count`` is the number of rows that flipped state — for
bulk-mark-expired this represents rows whose ``is_expired`` flipped
True, named ``paused_count`` for shape parity with bulk-pause so the
dashboard can render both with one component.

``skipped_count`` covers rows already in the requested state (the
common idempotent re-call) AND rows where the ``set_*`` call
returned 0 due to a race with another writer. The two cases are
indistinguishable on the wire by design — the operator only cares
about the totals.

``errors`` carries per-item failure rows; an empty list is the
happy path. ``requested_count`` is ``affected + skipped + len(errors)``,
redundant on the wire but useful so operators don't have to add
three numbers in their head.
BulkOperationResult.title: BulkOperationResult

BulkSelectorBody.description:
XOR selector for bulk pause / mark-expired.

Exactly one of ``platform`` / ``user_emails`` must be set. The
model_validator enforces the XOR at the pydantic layer so a 422
fires before the router body even runs — the service-layer call
never sees a malformed selector.

``user_emails`` is capped at 1000 entries per call (see module
docstring). The cap is enforced via Field's ``max_length`` so the
422 carries a precise field path.
BulkSelectorBody.title: BulkSelectorBody

CredentialDetail.description:
Summary plus the set of keys inside the encrypted payload.

``payload_readable=False`` means the Fernet decrypt failed; the UI
should surface that as a credential health signal rather than
treating it as a missing row.
CredentialDetail.title: CredentialDetail

DaemonConfig.description:
Daemon-level settings.

Env precedence is handled by pydantic-settings. The overlay is applied by
:func:`load_config` after initial construction.
DaemonConfig.title: DaemonConfig

DestructiveActionBody.description:
Body schema for actions that delete data or cancel in-flight work.

``confirm`` must equal the target identifier exactly. Mismatch
rejects with 422 so a typo can't fat-finger the action. ``reason``
is required so every destructive audit row carries operator context.
DestructiveActionBody.title: DestructiveActionBody

ErrorItem.description:
One entry in the merged errors feed.

Three ``kind`` values are emitted: ``dead_letter``, ``failed_sync``,
``expired_credential``. Fields are optional across kinds because each
source carries a different subset (e.g. ``sync_id`` is only on
failed_sync rows).
ErrorItem.title: ErrorItem

FernetRotationResponse.description:
Per-row counts from the rotation pass.

Field names mirror :class:`RotationResult` so the same shape is
documented in OpenAPI as the underlying dataclass.
FernetRotationResponse.title: FernetRotationResponse

ForceRefreshResult.description:
Outcome of one on-demand Teams refresh.

Returned only when the refresh succeeded or the credential was
detected as expired; transient failures surface as 502 and never
reach the response model.
ForceRefreshResult.title: ForceRefreshResult

ForceSyncQueueItem.description:
One row from ``force_sync_requests`` decoded for the wire.

``requested_by_actor`` is best-effort: the table stores ``reason`` but
not the actor identity. We surface the ``reason`` field under its
own column AND the most-recently-written audit row's ``actor`` for
the matching ``sync.force_requested`` action so the dashboard can
render "operator X queued this Y minutes ago". The audit join is a
LEFT JOIN — a row without a matching audit entry (somehow inserted
out-of-band) still lists with ``requested_by_actor=None``.
ForceSyncQueueItem.title: ForceSyncQueueItem

ItemDetail.description:
Per-item drawer payload.

``payload`` and ``raw_payload`` are intentionally typed as
``dict[str, Any]`` — the normalized payload's shape varies per
connector and content type; pinning a sub-schema would force a
Pydantic model per connector + content type, which the registry
resolves at runtime, not build time. The dashboard renders these as
a tree view rather than typed cards, so the loose shape matches the
consumer.
ItemDetail.title: ItemDetail

LifecycleConfig.description:
TTL prune windows for daemon-owned tables (slice 12).

Each ``*_retention_days`` field is the maximum age of rows kept in
the corresponding table before the lifecycle prune loop deletes
them. Set any field to ``0`` to disable that prune entirely (the
loop driver treats ``0`` as "skip this pass" rather than "delete
everything"). The interval governs how often the loop wakes up;
1 hour matches the existing log-retention loop.

Defaults:

* sync_history: 30 days (matches operator-incident review window)
* dead_letter: 90 days (long enough to spot recurring issues)
* audit_log: 365 days (compliance default)
LifecycleConfig.title: LifecycleConfig

LogEntry.description:
One decoded row from the ``logs`` table.

``context`` is the parsed ``fields_json`` payload so the wire format
only carries the decoded context, not both the raw string and the
parsed dict.
LogEntry.title: LogEntry

LogLevel.description: Log levels we persist. Matches the canonicalised uppercase form.
LogLevel.title: LogLevel

LogList.description:
Wrapper around the per-sync log rows.

The ``items`` field carries the same :class:`LogEntry` shape the
primary ``/api/logs`` endpoint returns; this convenience wrapper
exists only so a frontend that already knows a sync_id doesn't have
to assemble the query string itself.
LogList.title: LogList

OkResponse.description:
Trivial ``{"ok": true}`` body returned by mutation endpoints that
have no other payload to surface.
OkResponse.title: OkResponse

OpsConfig.description:
Operator safety switches. Persistent via the overlay.

Shadow mode suppresses content writes through :class:`PostgresContentSink`
so a full fetch cycle runs end-to-end (adapter, normalization, cursor
updates via the sync-state path) without producing visible content in
the shared ``ingested_items`` table. It's intended for testing schema
changes or credential rotations without downstream consumers seeing
half-processed data.

Intentionally in scope: content writes (``upsert``/``upsert_batch``) and
the content-triggered sync_history completion entry. Intentionally OUT
of scope: audit_log, logs, dead_letter, and failed_sync writers — those
are observability surfaces and must keep working so the shadow run is
still inspectable from the dashboard.
OpsConfig.title: OpsConfig

OverlayMap.description: Flat dotted-key-to-value map as stored in ``config_overlay``.
OverlayMap.title: OverlayMap

OverlayResetResult.description:
Outcome of POST /api/config/overlay/reset-all.

``cleared_keys`` is the list of overlay keys that existed pre-reset
and were deleted by this call. Empty list when the overlay was
already empty (idempotent re-call).
OverlayResetResult.title: OverlayResetResult

PauseResult.description:
Outcome of a (un)pause action.

``rows_affected`` counts rows that flipped state; ``rows_total`` is
the total rows in scope (one for credential-level actions, the
user's full credential count for user-level actions).
PauseResult.title: PauseResult

PlatformPauseConfig.description:
Per-platform pause switches. Set via the overlay to temporarily stop
syncs for a single platform without disabling it outright.

Distinct from :class:`PlatformToggles`'s ``*_enabled`` flags: ``enabled``
is treated as permanent configuration (disables the adapter end-to-end,
drops forced syncs); ``paused`` is treated as a transient operator pause
so the scheduler skips the platform but leaves credentials and routing
intact. The dashboard's V10 ops pane toggles this.
PlatformPauseConfig.title: PlatformPauseConfig

ReadyChecks.description:
Per-check status surface inside the ``/ready`` body.

Each field is a fixed enum so dashboards can colour-code without
string-matching free-form messages.
ReadyChecks.title: ReadyChecks

ReadyResponse.description:
Readiness probe payload. ``status`` is ``ok`` only when every
dependent check is non-degraded.
ReadyResponse.title: ReadyResponse

ReplayDeadLetterResult.description:
Outcome of POST /api/actions/dead_letter/{email}/{platform}/replay.

``counter_preserved`` is True by design — the contrast with the
``clear`` action is the one piece of operator-facing information
the wire shape needs to surface, so callers can branch on it
without reading docs. (See ``maintenance_service.replay_dead_letter``
for why preservation matters.)
ReplayDeadLetterResult.title: ReplayDeadLetterResult

RunningSync.description:
One in-flight sync as observed in ``sync_history``.

``elapsed_seconds`` is computed at response time (now - started_at)
rather than persisted: a long-running sync's elapsed value updates
every poll without requiring a writer to refresh the row.

``items_fetched_so_far`` is intentionally nullable: the daemon's
sync_profiles row only lands at log_complete, and there's no
incremental counter on the running row today. Callers should treat
None as "live count not available" rather than zero — the field is
declared so a future enhancement can fill it in without a wire-shape
break.
RunningSync.title: RunningSync

RunningSyncList.description: Wrapper for :class:`RunningSync` so OpenAPI gets a stable name.
RunningSyncList.title: RunningSyncList

SentryConfig.description:
Optional Sentry/GlitchTip error-tracker integration.

When ``dsn`` is non-empty the daemon initialises ``sentry_sdk`` at
startup. Unhandled exceptions, ``logger.exception/error`` calls, and
FastAPI request failures flow to the configured GlitchTip/Sentry
instance automatically. Leave ``dsn`` empty to disable — the daemon
still boots, just without external error forwarding.

``public_url`` is the browser-facing base URL of the GlitchTip UI
(e.g. ``http://localhost:8000``). The dashboard reads it via
/api/settings/about and renders a "Open in GlitchTip" link on the
Errors page. It's separate from ``dsn`` because the DSN is an
ingest endpoint and the public URL is where a human clicks.
SentryConfig.title: SentryConfig

SyncHistoryItem.description:
One decoded row from ``sync_history``.

``stats`` / ``cursor_before`` / ``cursor_after`` were stored as JSON
strings and come back either as a parsed object or ``None``; we keep
them permissive because the shape varies per connector.
SyncHistoryItem.title: SyncHistoryItem

SyncProfile.description:
``sync_profiles`` row decoded. ``per_scope`` is the parsed
``per_scope_json`` (or ``None`` when the JSON fails to decode);
``per_scope_json`` stays in the payload so clients can still read
the raw text if they need it.
SyncProfile.title: SyncProfile

TeamsRefreshConfig.description: Bulk-refresh cycle for Teams tokens using the headless Playwright pool.
TeamsRefreshConfig.title: TeamsRefreshConfig

UserItemRow.description:
Row in the Contributions tab — one IngestedItem scoped to the user.

Fields pulled from the JSON `payload` blob (title, course_name,
published_at) are projected up for the table view. `raw_payload` is
intentionally omitted — fetch the item detail endpoint for that.
UserItemRow.title: UserItemRow

UserScheduleOverride.description: Shape of one ``user_schedule_overrides`` row on the wire.
UserScheduleOverride.title: UserScheduleOverride

UserScheduleOverrideBody.description:
Editable fields of an override row. Excludes user_email (URL) and
updated_at (server-populated).
UserScheduleOverrideBody.title: UserScheduleOverrideBody

UserStats.description:
Aggregates for the User detail → Overview tab.

``cursors`` is a free-form JSON object: each platform maps to a
scope -> cursor map, where the cursor shape varies per connector
(Teams' delta token, Moodle's last-fetched id, etc.). Kept loose so
a connector can evolve its cursor format without a schema migration.
UserStats.title: UserStats

WhyNotRunningResponse.description:
Diagnostic explanation for why a single (email, platform) is
or is not running.

``next_due_at`` is None when the credential is permanently blocked
(paused, expired) — there is no future tick that would unblock it
without operator action, so a timestamp would be misleading. For
transient blocks (suppressed, not_due, running), it's the wall-clock
moment the scheduler would reconsider the row.

``reason`` is a human-readable amplification of ``blocked_by``:
``"credential is paused"``, ``"global pause is active"``, etc. The
enum carries the machine-readable bit; the message makes the
dashboard's empty-state copy useful.
WhyNotRunningResponse.title: WhyNotRunningResponse

ingestion__daemon__api__routers__about_r.description:
Build + runtime metadata payload.

All fields are required strings/ints so the wire shape is stable —
a missing build-time env var resolves to ``"unknown"`` rather than
omitting the key. This keeps client codegen (TypeScript) simple:
no nullable fields to unwrap.
ingestion__daemon__api__routers__about_r.title: AboutResponse

post.description:
Re-encrypt every credential row to the new Fernet primary.

The new key MUST already be in the daemon's environment as
``ENDPOINT_FERNET_KEY_NEW``. Returns per-row counts so the
caller can confirm a clean rotation (``failed=0``) before
flipping ``ENDPOINT_FERNET_KEY`` to drop the old key.

Idempotent: a second call after a partial rotation only touches
rows still on the old key. The per-row UPDATE is keyed on the
pre-rotation ciphertext so a concurrent refresh-loop write
landing mid-rotation lands as ``raced`` rather than overwriting
the fresh payload.

get.description: Return the fully merged config (defaults + env + overlay).

post.description:
Clear every overlay key in one operation. Idempotent.

Snapshot the full overlay map BEFORE deletion so the audit row's
``before`` payload preserves the pre-reset state — operators can
reconstruct the prior config from the audit log alone if a reset
turns out to have been a mistake.

The ``deleted`` loop is per-key rather than a single SQL TRUNCATE
because the existing :class:`LocalStore` only exposes per-key
deletes; a future store-level batch delete would let this become
truly atomic. Today the window between deleting key 1 and key N
is small (in-process, single-thread under the write lock).

The blocked-by priority follows :func:`_blocked_by` for global +
platform + per-credential states, then surfaces ``running`` /
``not_due`` / ``none`` based on the live sync_history + interval
computation. ``next_due_at`` is None for permanent blocks (paused,
expired, platform_disabled) and a timestamp for transient ones.
Static info about the running daemon.

Per-platform liveness probes. Cached in memory for
``_HEALTH_TTL_SECONDS`` so the Overview page can poll cheaply.
Effective retention settings as the daemon is running them.
File size + per-table row counts + oldest rows in the hot tables.

schema.title: Response List Syncs V1 Syncs Get

get.description:
Every sync currently in flight (sync_history.state='running').

Reads only from ``sync_history``: the worker pool tracks tasks in
memory, but the canonical source for "is this sync still running"
is the persisted row — a worker that crashed without patching its
row is reconciled at next daemon boot
(:meth:`SqliteSyncLogger.reconcile_orphaned_running`).

Logs for a single sync run by ``sync_id``.

404 when ``sync_id`` doesn't exist in ``sync_history`` — telling an
operator their typoed UUID returns "no logs" would be confusing. A
valid sync_id with zero log rows still returns 200 with an empty
list (a brand-new run that hasn't logged yet).
List users with their per-platform summary. Paginated by user_email.

tab in the dashboard. Items with no attribution (telegram, legacy
rows before the `fetched_by_user_email` column landed) are excluded.
